description: ASML's pilot program to service older lithography machines in China via its Belgian subsidiary escalates into a broader de facto loosening of export controls, as other EU-based suppliers quietly follow suit. The U.S. responds with legal threats and diplomatic pressure, but the precedent of selective compliance fractures the unity of the export regime. This creates a grey market for dual-use servicing that the EU struggles to regulate uniformly, exposing tensions between industrial sovereignty and transatlantic alignment.
